newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia's Trepca to raise metals output - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia's Trepca to raise metals output - agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Rudarsko Metalurski Kombinat Trepca metal works plans to produce around 2.35 million tonnes of lead and zinc ore from its mines in 1997, the official news agency Tanjug reported on Tuesday.
It plans to produce 71,180 tonnes of lead and 108,472 tonnes of zinc concentrate this year, Tanjug quoted Trepca sources as saying.
No-one at Trepca was immediately available for comment.

Trepca's two metallurgy plants are expected to produce 80,200 tonnes of lead, 70,000 kg of silver, 102 kg of gold, 52,510 tonnes of zinc, 121,211 tonnes of sulphuric acid and 129 tonnes of cadmium this year.
This would be nearly two and a half times last year's output of metals, the report said.

The Trepca group, based in Serbia's southern province of Kosovo, is the country's largest metals complex, comprising 14 lead and zinc mines, nine flotation and two metallurgy plants, and 14 factories. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
